board.title: Hashing
board.author: Julius Boateng
board.description: Hashes are used everywhere in computer science. They are used for efficient data structures, data integrity checks, and cryptographic security. This puzzle explores common hashing techniques and applications.

clues.question: Fixed-length value produced by a cryptographic hash function like MD5 or SHA-256
Hash ___; two distinct inputs produce the same hash value; inevitable due to the pigeonhole principle
___ resistance; property of cryptographic hash functions where finding an input that produces a given hash value is computationally infeasible
___ filter; probabilistic data structure using multiple hash functions to test if an item belongs to a set; false positives, no false negatives
___ hash; hashing technique that efficiently updates a hash value for overlapping substrings of data
___ tree; hash tree where each parent node is the hash of its children; root summarizes the entire dataset
___-sensitive hashing; hashing technique that intentionally causes similar input items to collide; used for similarity search
___ hashing; technique that randomly chooses from a family of hash functions; reduces the impact of unlucky input distributions
___ hashing; hashing technique where resizing a hash table remaps a small fraction of keys; used to minimize key reassignment in distributed systems
Value derived from data to detect changes during storage or transmission; verifies integrity but not authenticity
___ effect; cryptographic property where a small input change produces a drastically different hash
Random value added to an input before hashing; gives identical inputs different hashes and protects against precomputed table attacks
___ paradox; probability phenomenon showing hash collisions become likely after roughly the square root of the number of possible hash values
___ hashing; guarantees no collisions for a fixed set of keys; possible because the key set is known in advance
Hashing algorithm for estimating the similarity of two sets by comparing signatures built from minimum hash values
Data structure that stores key-value pairs by mapping keys to array indices using hash functions; handles collisions via chaining or open addressing
